subject: Request: sprint carveout for AtlasEdge low-latency connector
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sasha Ivanov <sasha@atlasedge.com>, Priya Rao <priya@atlasedge.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: sprint carveout for AtlasEdge low-latency connector

Team —

Quick context: AtlasEdge (Sasha/Priya) have a proof-of-concept running and binding the POC success to a go/no-go decision this quarter. Primary ask: they need a direct low-latency connector (webhook+socket hybrid) so their inference loop stays under 120ms median. This is blocking terms finalization — they want a 6-month reserved capacity commit once the POC proves latency.

Why this is urgent:
- Deal size: ~$1.2M ARR if they convert (see SOW attached).
- Timeline: POC demo scheduled 2027-09-22 (customer expects a short-latency demo).

What we need from Product & Eng:
1) Feasibility: can we deliver a hardened connector that reduces routing/handshake overhead to meet ~120ms median?
2) Scope: what minimal feature set and safety/telemetry guardrails are required for an MVP so we can ship in a sprint carveout?
3) ETA & risk: estimate dev effort, whether this must be a canary-only feature, and any capacity implications (GPU affinity, dedicated lanes).

Attachments: AtlasEdge_SOW_v4.pdf, atlasedge_latency_profile.csv (customer-provided). HubSpot deal link below.

Asks: can we get a Product decision and an Eng feasibility note by EOD tomorrow (2027-09-08)? I realize this is tight — Rishi, can you triage resource availability?

Thanks —
Maya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sasha Ivanov <sasha@atlasedge.com>, Priya Rao <priya@atlasedge.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: sprint carveout for AtlasEdge low-latency connector

Maya — thanks for the clear note and attachments. High level reaction from Product: the ask is reasonable for an MVP if we constrain scope tightly. Two immediate clarifying questions before we commit to a sprint carveout:

1) Traffic profile: is this transactional single-request-per-session or long-lived streaming? The attached latency_profile looks spiky — need to confirm steady-state qps for the POC.
2) Security/Compliance: do they require customer-managed keys or VPC-only ingress for the POC? That would materially change effort.

If the answers are transactional, low-qps and no CMK/VPC requirement for POC, we could propose a targeted sprint carveout for a brokered connector (no full VPC). Engineering would need a 2-week focused cycle + 1-week stabilization for canary. Markus / Eng — can you validate feasibility and a more concrete timeline?

Also tagging Monica for success plan alignment and legal redline awareness.

— Irene
VP, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sasha Ivanov <sasha@atlasedge.com>, Priya Rao <priya@atlasedge.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: sprint carveout for AtlasEdge low-latency connector

Irene / Maya — quick engineering readout. Short answer: feasible, with constraints. Details below.

Summary of approach (MVP):
- Brokered connector implemented as a socket session manager in the serving layer to avoid extra HTTP proxy hops.
- Prefix caching + direct KV cache warm-up for repeated short contexts.
- Dedicated lightweight routing lane (soft-affinity) to avoid cross-tenant queues. Not full reserved capacity but a prioritized path.

Estimated scope & timeline:
- Design spike: 3 business days (RD-4521 created).
- Implementation: 8 business days (2 engineers, one backend infra, one runtime) — target branch and canary.
- Stabilization & observability: 3 business days (telemetry, SLAs in Console).
Total: ~14 business days from start. Can compress to 10 business days if we accept reduced telemetry and manual rollback procedures.

Risk/Blockers:
- If customer requires CMK or VPC egress, add 2–3 weeks and security review.
- GPU affinity reservations for 6-month commit is separate procurement work; product needs to confirm if they require persistent dedicated instances vs reserved throughput lanes.
- Load testing required to ensure median <120ms — customer profile must be representative.

Ask from Sales/Product to Eng to proceed:
- Final confirmation on traffic profile + security posture from AtlasEdge (Maya to confirm).
- Approval for a two-week focused carveout (Markus will need a sprint slot and 2 engineers).

I can start the design spike tomorrow if we get alignment.

— Markus
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sasha Ivanov <sasha@atlasedge.com>, Priya Rao <priya@atlasedge.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: sprint carveout for AtlasEdge low-latency connector

Thanks Markus — good breakdown. AtlasEdge confirms:
- Traffic: transactional (single request per inference loop), bursty during demo but steady-state < 20 qps for POC.
- Security: for the POC they will accept brokered connections (no CMK or VPC) but will want CMK/VPC during production only if we proceed to reserved capacity.

Given that, can we propose a compressed plan for a 10-business-day delivery (Markus's compressed option) to hit the 2027-09-22 demo? Markus — can you confirm resource availability for tomorrow's spike? Rishi, can you confirm we have capacity to pull two engineers for a short carveout?

Thanks —
Maya

Subject: Re: Request: sprint carveout for AtlasEdge low-latency connector

All — quick operations confirmation and next steps from CS/legal side.

1) I'm locking a provisional two-week engineering window starting Monday (2027-09-13) — Markus, please confirm you can commit the two engineers and that RD-4521 covers the design spike.
2) Legal: I'll start an expedited SOW review for the POC terms in AtlasEdge_SOW_v4.pdf; expect a redline by 2027-09-10 EOD.
3) Demo plan: Maya, can you get AtlasEdge to provide a representative set of 20 qps load traces and a consolidated acceptance criteria doc for the demo (latency percentile targets + failure mode expectations)? Put those in the confluence spec link above.

If all confirmed, Product and Eng can run the spike + implementation to the compressed 10-business-day path and we will aim to canary the feature into the demo environment starting 2027-09-20.

Thanks —
Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
